slides.alt: The German airship Hindenburg, its tail engulfed in a huge ball of flame, hangs nose-up beside the Lakehurst mooring mast as tiny figures run below.
slides.credit: Photograph: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.alt: Editorial slide headlined '97 people were on board', noting 36 passengers and 61 crew on a transatlantic crossing from Frankfurt.
Editorial slide headlined 'It was filled with hydrogen', explaining that the gas provided lift and the outer skin was treated with a flammable dope.
Editorial slide showing the number 34 and the line 'Seconds from first flame to the ground', with the note that the fire began near the rear upper fin at 7:25 p.m.
Editorial slide headlined 'Thirty-six people died', noting thirty-five aboard and one on the ground, with sixty-two survivors and a cause still officially undetermined.
Editorial slide headlined 'It ended the airship era', noting no commercial rigid airships were built after 1937 and the Lakehurst mooring mast still stands.
Dark closing card with the Cluefolio wordmark, the message 'Follow for the machines that changed history, and the failures that ended them', and a button reading FOLLOW @CLUEFOLIO.
